title: Target sales climb 7.1% in third quarter as it lifts forecast
h1: Target's third-quarter sales rose 7.1% on stronger customer traffic, and the retailer raised its full-year forecast
description: Target reported November 18, 2026 that third-quarter net sales rose 7.1% to $27.1 billion, with comparable sales up 5.6% and a higher full-year profit forecast.
standfirst: A 5% rise in customer transactions helped the retailer beat Wall Street's sales expectations. Tariff refunds added 50 cents to quarterly earnings per share and also lifted the full-year outlook.
keywords: Target third quarter earnings 2026, Target comparable sales, Target raises guidance, Michael Fiddelke, Target tariff refunds, retail earnings November 2026
takeaways: Net sales rose 7.1% to $27.1 billion, and comparable sales rose 5.6%.
Earnings were $2.65 per share, including about $0.50 from tariff refunds.
Target now expects full-year earnings of $10.65 to $11.40 per share, up from $9.90 to $10.90.
body: Target said on November 18 that net sales rose 7.1% to $27.1 billion in its fiscal third quarter, as comparable sales climbed 5.6%. The company also lifted its full-year forecast, according to its earnings release. CNBC described the result as the retailer's best sales growth in five years.
Analysts had expected revenue of $26.56 billion and comparable sales growth of 3.8%, based on LSEG and StreetAccount figures cited by CNBC.

Traffic did most of the work. Comparable transactions rose 5.0%, while the average purchase grew just 0.6%, the company reported. Comparable sales increased 4.6% in stores and 9.8% in digital channels. CNBC reported that beauty sales rose 9% and food and beverage sales rose nearly 7%, and that Target cut prices on about 2,000 more items during the quarter.
"The changes we've made across our assortment and guest experience are adding up," Chief Executive Michael Fiddelke told reporters, CNBC reported.

Operating income reached $1.7 billion, and earnings were $2.65 per share, compared with $1.51 on a reported basis and $1.78 on an adjusted basis a year earlier. Those results include $301 million in pretax tariff refunds, worth $0.50 per share. Without the refunds, the company said, reported earnings per share would have grown 42% and adjusted earnings per share 21%.

Target now expects full-year net sales growth of around 6%, one point above its earlier range. It projects earnings of $10.65 to $11.40 per share, up from the $9.90 to $10.90 range CNBC cited as prior guidance. The new forecast includes about $2.14 per share from refunds recognized so far and leaves out any future refunds. The company also plans capital spending of $5 billion to $6 billion in 2027 as it heads into the holiday season.
